subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust contract should OpenClaw adopt for source authority, review state, expiration, and influence policy across default memory, QMD, Active Memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin SDK boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the schema, config surface, source-of-truth assignment, and security enforcement model are product/security decisions that automation should not invent.

options.title: Design native trust policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and define structured source trust metadata, storage versus influence policy, review/expiration gates, and retrieval weighting before implementation.

options.title: Stage behind provenance MVP
options.body: Use the open durable provenance tracker as the prerequisite and implement trust tiers only after source lineage and promotion semantics are settled.

options.title: Defer to plugin/MCP path
options.body: Document external memory systems such as world-model-mcp as optional integrations while leaving OpenClaw native memory unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Design native trust policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define structured source trust metadata, storage versus influence policy, review/expiration gates, and retrieval weighting before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest verified current-main and prior-review signal on the memory host SDK and memory-core contract boundary.
